independent_computation.step_0_what_the_leaf_is: The leaf is the `owner` attribute of the 18th entry (index 17) of the coupled scenario's support-event ledger. `support_events` is the engine's heal/shield/support ledger: the practice corpus serializes entries of this family as `"kind": "support_shield"` with fields source / shield / applied / received / absorbed (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json, ids e9-e8-annie-molten-shield, e9-e8-serpents-fang-shield-cut, e9-item-fimbulwinter-everlasting), and the E8d worklist confirms the same shape is reused for ally-support heals/shields ('the ledger already tracks support_shield_received / support heals from items — reuse the same event shape', data/worklists/e8d-task.md). `owner` therefore denotes the roster participant the support event is attributed to.

Black Cleaver (data/items.json id 3071).Carve: Dealing physical damage to an enemy champion applies a stack of Carve for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts 6% armor reduction, up to 30% at 5 stacks.
Black Cleaver (data/items.json id 3071).Fervor: Dealing physical damage grants you 20 bonus movement speed for 2 seconds.
Black Cleaver (data/items.json id 3071).support_character: Carve's armor reduction is a debuff on the target and therefore benefits every ally attacking that target — a genuine cross-participant (support) effect owned by the Cleaver holder. It grants no heal or shield.

If the target is a champion, inflict them with Expose Weakness for 4 seconds, causing them to take 8%/5% increased damage from all sources (1.5 second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Bloodsong (data/items.json id 3877).support_character: Expose Weakness amplifies damage 'from all sources', i.e. it is a team-wide amp owned by the Bloodsong holder. Bloodsong's only heal-family output is the 75% base health-regen line (item-atoms/3877.json carries heal-shield.health-regeneration and heal-shield.max-health-increase-restores-current); it grants no ally heal or shield.

step_1_what_the_two_named_items_actually.conclusion_of_step_1: Every support-family effect this scenario can produce (Carve shred, Expose Weakness amp, item health/regen) is emitted BY a specific roster participant — the item holder. None of them is an ownerless, participant-free effect. There is no effect in either item's cached wiki text whose provenance is a non-champion entity (the only non-champion unit either item creates is Bloodsong's Stealth Ward, which produces vision, not a support-ledger heal/shield).

independent_computation.step_2_structural_requirement_from_the_d: data/atoms/autoresearch-review.md §3.2 ('Ledger fix (multi-target heals re-priced by roster index) — sound') states the coupled ledger prices support events by participant index: 'the coupled ledger re-prices defenders past the first (defender_index > 0)' and 'Index semantics match the legacy attack groups everywhere: allied attackers -> enemies indexed from 0; enemy attackers -> [main, *allies] with main at 0 and allies at 1+.' A support event that carries no participant attribution cannot be placed in that indexing at all — it can be neither re-priced nor routed to a ledger. Attribution is therefore load-bearing for exactly this scenario family (a *_roster coupled fight). An absent `owner` is not a value the coupled ledger design can consume.
independent_computation.step_3_which_participant: The scenario name pairs the two items in one label ('cleaver_bloodsong_roster') with 'roster' as the qualifier for the allies list (cf. the corpus scenario cp21-ziggs-outer-blast, which uses setup.allies for the roster). The most consistent reading is: the main participant carries Black Cleaver + Bloodsong (legal with role=support and the quest complete — the engine's role_quest_complete flag is the gate named in data/worklists/issues-c-task.md item 3), and the roster allies are the beneficiaries of the shred/amp. Under that reading, the emitter — and hence the owner — of the item-sourced support events is the main participant, i.e. exactly the old value 'main'.
independent_computation.step_4_verdict_logic: new_value (<absent>) is rejected because (a) no cached effect of either item is ownerless, and (b) the documented coupled-ledger design requires per-participant attribution for support events. Given the field must be present, the only participant supported by the evidence for these item-sourced events is the main participant. Hence 'main' is the defensible value and the removal is a loss of provenance, not a correction. This also matches the repo's stated convention that unmatched provenance is 'named rather than dropped' (data/README.md, sourceWarnings row).

NEGATIVE EVIDENCE: the document's §5 formula-audit table covers resistance, penetration, growth, AS, haste, DoT, on-hit stacking, shields, grey health, revive and the BC `average_reduction` Cesaro-mean approximation, but contains no identity, convention or invariant governing support-event serialization or event ownership. Grep for 'owner' in docs/math-foundations.md returns nothing; grep for '"owner"' across all of data/ returns nothing.

limitations: No file in the permitted evidence tree (data/ + docs/math-foundations.md) defines the `owner` field, its allowed values, or the conditions under which it may be omitted; the scenario definition itself lives outside the tree (scripts/), so the roster composition and item assignment could not be read, only inferred from the scenario name and the corpus' roster convention.

Alternative hypothesis not excludable from this evidence tree: the support-event list may have shifted by one (an inserted or removed earlier event), in which case index 17 now addresses a different event and the leaf-level 'main -> absent' delta is an indexing artifact rather than a semantic change. Sibling leaves at support_events[16..18] (kind/source/amount) would settle this; they were not part of this oracle's assignment.

Second alternative: if the roster assigns Bloodsong to a support ALLY rather than to the main participant, then the correct owner is that ally and both values would be wrong (verdict would become both_wrong). Nothing in data/ fixes the assignment; the single-build reading of the scenario name was used.
